analysis.title: Americas Business & Information Services: October temp staffing trends improve but recovery remains gradual
key_insights: US temp penetration rose to 1.59% in October from 1.58% in September. It is still the fifth lowest reading in six years, below the 1.92% pre-COVID level and three standard deviations below the 2.09% peak of February 2022.

US temp jobs rose 3.0% y/y in October, up from 1.4% in September. Jobs rose 18.6k m/m after a 5.6k decline in September, and prior months were revised up, leaving September temp jobs 20.6k higher than first reported.
Total US temp jobs were 2,526k in October against 2,917k in January 2020. GS says the gap reflects both cyclical and structural declines.

Temp wage growth was 5.1% y/y in September, above the 10-year average of 4.7%. Permanent wage growth was 3.2% y/y in September and 3.1% in October. Historically, temp bill-pay spreads move with temp wage growth, so the wage backdrop could support staffing gross margins, but pricing strength has not come with a volume recovery.
GS expects the cyclical recovery to be less robust than in prior cycles because about 55% of US temp roles are white-collar and exposed to AI-driven disintermediation.
Temp staffing has historically led the broader macro and labor market by 2-4 quarters, though strong labor supply growth may have lengthened the current lead time.

GS keeps a Sell on Robert Half (PT $33) on white-collar exposure and its dependence on a stronger volume recovery. Robert Half's Talent Solutions grew 2% y/y in 3Q, its first growth since 2022, but contract volumes are still negative and contract growth is pricing-driven.

GS keeps a Neutral on Manpower (PT $50). Revenue growth slowed to 5% y/y CC in 3Q from 6% in 2Q. US Experis returned to growth, but gross margins are pressured by mix and 4Q guidance implies positive consensus revenue revisions with negative consensus EPS revisions.

GS stays positive on Korn Ferry (Buy, PT $95). New business grew 12% y/y CC and cross-solution referrals reached 29% of fee revenue in F1Q. AMS adds contracted revenue, and the company targets AMS adjusted EBITDA of $140mn from about $100mn within 12 months, with EPS accretion expected in the first full year after the close.

market_movers.rationale: Improving organic demand, cross-selling and AMS increase contracted revenue visibility and should support growth and earnings accretion. Target is 14.5x NTM + 1YR EPS of $6.52.
Improving demand and share gains are offset by gross margin pressure and limited near-term earnings conversion. Target is 8.5x NTM + 1YR EPS of $5.88.
White-collar staffing exposure and dependence on a volume recovery that has not arrived. Target is 13.5x NTM + 1YR EPS estimate of $2.42.

sector_views.rationale: Temp indicators are stabilizing but remain near multi-year lows. GS calls the recovery nascent and gradual, with AI exposure of white-collar roles a structural drag.

earnings_insights: RHI reported 3Q26 (quarter ended Sept-26) Talent Solutions growth of 2% y/y, with contract staffing +1% and permanent placement +6%. Company guidance for 4Q Talent Solutions is 3% y/y at the midpoint.
RHI Protiviti declined 3% y/y in 3Q (reported). GS expects it to turn positive in 4Q on AML remediation demand.

MAN reported 3Q26 revenue growth of 5% y/y CC against 6% in 2Q. GS says 4Q guidance points to positive consensus revenue revisions and negative consensus EPS revisions, reflecting limited revenue conversion and a higher tax rate.
KFY F1Q (reported): new business grew 12% y/y CC, new business productivity rose 14% y/y, and cross-solution referrals were 29% of fee revenue, up 300 bps y/y.

GS estimates (not reported): KFY adjusted EPS $5.69 for FY Apr-27E and $6.32 for FY Apr-28E. MAN adjusted EPS $3.59 for 2026E and $4.89 for 2027E. RHI adjusted EPS $1.28 for 2026E and $1.98 for 2027E.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from 1.58% in September but near historically depressed levels, so employer reliance on temp labor remains limited.
Up from 1.4% in September. A gradual recovery in temp staffing, still subdued.
Follows a revised 5.6k decline in September.

macro_indicators.indicator: US temp average hourly earnings y/y
macro_indicators.interpretation: Above the 10-year average of 4.7% and above permanent wage growth, which could support staffing gross margins.

macro_indicators.indicator: US permanent worker average hourly earnings y/y
macro_indicators.interpretation: Below the 10-year average of 3.9%. It was 3.2% in September.

risk_factors: AI-driven disintermediation of white-collar temp roles, which are about 55% of US temp jobs.
Temp volumes have not recovered even as pricing improves. Contract staffing volumes at Robert Half are still down y/y.
Manpower gross margin pressure from growth skewing to lower-margin enterprise staffing, a slowdown in European manufacturing, weakness in the Experis brand, and FX.
Korn Ferry near-term earnings dilution from AMS acquisition amortization, interest expense and share issuance, plus integration, competitive, macro and FX risks.
Upside risks to the Sell and Neutral views: stronger macro, rising temp penetration, improving labor markets, wage inflation, Protiviti growth and operating leverage.

Exhibit 3 plots Robert Half revenue growth against US temp worker growth from 1Q08 to 3Q26 with R of 0.90.

Exhibit 5 shows temp wage growth at 5.1% in September against all-worker wage growth of 3.1% in October.
geopolitical: Macro and geopolitical uncertainty limits discretionary activity and concentrates hiring in mission-critical initiatives, as cited in the Robert Half discussion.

tension_points.bull_case: Temp penetration rose to 1.59%, temp jobs growth accelerated to 3.0% y/y with upward revisions, and temp wage growth of 5.1% y/y supports staffing gross margins. Robert Half Talent Solutions returned to growth and Manpower's US Experis returned to growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Penetration is the fifth lowest in six years and about 55% of temp roles are white-collar and exposed to AI disintermediation. Pricing has not come with volume recovery, contract volumes at Robert Half are still negative, and Manpower faces gross margin pressure and negative EPS revisions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The report names no break level. It says a sustained recovery in temp penetration would be a more constructive signal and would soften its cautious view.

theme_stances.key_argument: Temp indicators are improving but remain near multi-year lows, so the recovery is gradual and nascent.
The cyclical recovery may be less robust because a large share of temp roles are white-collar.
